```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  # Skip evaluation if tma / rENA are not available (e.g. CRAN check machines)
  eval = requireNamespace("tma",  quietly = TRUE) &&
         requireNamespace("rENA", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

This article walks through fitting a standard **ENA** (undirected) model and
an **ONA** (directed) model from the built-in `RS.data` dataset using the
`tma` and `rENA` packages, then rendering both as live interactive plots with
`qeviz`.

## Data and model setup

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(qeviz)
library(tma)
library(rENA)

data(RS.data)
```

Define the units, hand-over-hand (HOO) rules, and code set:

```{r model-spec}
units_by  <- c("Condition", "UserName")
codes     <- c(
  "Data", "Technical.Constraints", "Performance.Parameters",
  "Client.and.Consultant.Requests", "Design.Reasoning", "Collaboration"
)

hoo_rules <- tma::conversation_rules(
  (Condition %in% UNIT$Condition) & (GroupName %in% UNIT$GroupName)
)
```

Accumulate co-occurrence tensors and fit both models:

```{r accumulate, message=FALSE}
context_model <- tma::contexts(
  RS.data,
  units_by  = make.names(units_by),
  hoo_rules = hoo_rules
)

multidim_arr <- tma::context_tensor(
  RS.data,
  sender_cols    = NULL,
  receiver_cols  = NULL,
  default_window = 8,
  default_weight = 1
)

result_ena <- tma::accumulate(
  tensor        = multidim_arr,
  codes         = codes,
  context_model = context_model,
  ordered       = FALSE
)

result_ona <- tma::accumulate(
  tensor        = multidim_arr,
  codes         = codes,
  context_model = context_model,
  ordered       = TRUE
)

ena_set <- rENA::model(result_ena)
ona_set <- rENA::model(result_ona, directed = TRUE)
```

## Extract ModelData for qeviz

`qe_extract()` reads the rotation nodes, unit points, edge weights, and group
metadata from the set object and normalises them into the qeviz `ModelData`
format:

```{r extract}
ena_model <- qe_extract(ena_set, directed = FALSE)
ona_model <- qe_extract(ona_set, directed = TRUE)
```

## Standard ENA (undirected)

Edge thickness reflects co-occurrence weight; all edges are symmetric.
Both groups are displayed in overlay mode so their means and point clouds
can be compared directly.

```{r ena-plot, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
groups <- sapply(ena_model$groups$data, `[[`, ena_model$group_col)
htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(
  ena_model,
  graph_opts = list(
    group = groups[1],
    also  = groups[2]
  )
))
```

## ONA (directed)

Directed edges are rendered as tapered arrows whose apex points toward the
stronger directional contributor; thickness and opacity both scale with weight.

```{r ona-plot, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
groups <- sapply(ona_model$groups$data, `[[`, ona_model$group_col)
htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(
  ona_model,
  graph_opts = list(
    group = groups[1],
    also  = groups[2]
  )
))
```

## Exporting a standalone file

To share or archive a plot, write it to a self-contained HTML file — no
server, no internet connection required:

```{r export, eval=FALSE}
qe_export_html(ena_model, "ena_plot.html")
qe_export_html(ona_model, "ona_plot.html", title = "ONA — RS.data")
```

## Customising the graph

`graph_opts` accepts any `<qe-graph>` attribute:

```{r opts, eval=FALSE}
qe_fragment(
  ena_model,
  height     = "560px",
  graph_opts = list(
    "label-nodes"  = "auto",   # show node labels on hover only
    "label-points" = "on",     # always show unit labels
    height         = "540"
  )
)
```
